what: Same-host cost of recording typed writes in the sync engine, against the unchanged write path (sync off)

host.name: betelgeuse
host.sqlite: bundled, WAL, synchronous=FULL as the app opens it
host.conditions: shared development host with other sessions; no CPU pinning; one run

workload: tasks created with add_task, each with 1 KiB notes; then 200 renames (rename_task), each a durable save; then the database is reopened
findings: Saves stay within the budget: p95 under 4 ms with sync on at both sizes, no worse than sync off on this host.
Reopen replays the whole journal: 87.5 ms at 1,000 tasks, 605.5 ms at 10,000. It grows with history until checkpoints (#40) bound it.

Creating tasks with sync on costs about 41 ms each at 10,000 tasks against 7.5 ms with sync off, growing with the task count: each create finds its predecessor by key, and tasks have no index on sort_order or today_order. Within the save budget, but a measured scaling cost to remove.
Journal: about 1.4 KB per created task with 1 KiB notes, and the database file roughly 2.4x the sync-off size at 10,000 tasks. Retention is unbounded until #40.
limits: One run on one shared host; distributions are of 200 renames, not repeated runs.
Receiving updates and rebuilding rows were not measured here.
source_note: Measured on a branch commit whose crates/matters-core/src is identical to main at 9fcf1c5 (git diff shows no source change); the branch commit was later rebased.
